question: The proposed Colombian law amending and extending Law 418 of 1997 creates the category of ‘illegal armed groups or terrorists’. It could include groups without requiring them to have committed a terrorist act or to have a specific terrorist purpose. Their playing ‘significant roles’ in illicit economies and having the ‘capacity’ to commit such acts would suffice.

This approach differs from Directive (EU) 2017/5411, which requires a group to have a specific terrorist purpose and provides for safeguards for fundamental rights and the exclusion of impartial humanitarian action.

Such a broad definition in the proposed Colombian act could affect human rights defenders, lawyers, journalists, researchers and rural communities, particularly given the lack of safeguards for professional secrecy and the use of incentivised witnesses. 1.

In the light of the above, has the European External Action Service (EEAS) assessed the compatibility of this category with Directive (EU) 2017/541 and EU standards on legality and fundamental rights?

What guarantees has it demanded to ensure that EU cooperation with Colombia on security, justice and intelligence does not contribute to the surveillance, targeting or criminalisation of civil society and peaceful protest?
What measures will the EEAS take to make such cooperation conditional upon respect for international humanitarian law, human rights and the implementation of the peace agreement?

Directive (EU) 2017/541 of 15 March 2017 on combating terrorism and replacing Council Framework Decision 2002/475/JHA and amending Council Decision 2005/671/JHA (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2017/541/oj). 1
